questions.question: When should the seatbelt be fastened?
options: Only when travelling on public roads
Before releasing the park brake or selecting a gear
After the first work cycle
Only on slopes
questions.explanation: Fasten the belt before the machine is able to move and keep it fastened while it can move.

questions.question: The machine starts to tip over. What is the correct action?
options: Jump clear on the downhill side
Open the door and jump uphill
Stay in the seat with the belt fastened and brace yourself
Stand up to see where the machine will land
questions.explanation: The cab is built to protect you during a rollover. Jumping clear risks being crushed by the machine.

questions.question: What should you do before leaving the cab?
options: Leave the engine running and the bucket raised
Lower attachments, set the park brake, and engage the control lockout
Unfasten the belt while still moving to save time
Put the machine in neutral only
questions.explanation: Lowered attachments, the park brake, and the lockout stop unexpected movement while you are away.

questions.question: How should you climb in or out of the cab?
options: Face away from the machine and step down quickly
Jump from the tracks
Face the machine and keep three points of contact
Hold the door with one hand only
questions.explanation: Facing the machine with three points of contact prevents most falls on steps.

questions.question: You cannot see the area behind the machine. What should you do?
options: Stand up in the cab to look
Lean out of the door while reversing slowly
Stop and ask for a spotter
Unfasten the belt to turn around
questions.explanation: Stay in the seat and use a spotter. Leaning out puts you outside the protected space.
